English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
dissertation
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin dissertātiō, from dissertō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˌdɪsəˈteɪʃən/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (General American, Canada) IPA(key): /ˌdɪsɚˈteɪʃən/
  • (General Australian) IPA(key): /ˌdɪs.əˈtæɪ.ʃən/
  • Rhymes: -eɪʃən

Noun

[edit]

dissertation (plural dissertations)

  1. A formal exposition of a subject, especially a research paper that students write in order to complete the requirements for a doctoral degree in the US and a non-doctoral degree in the UK; a thesis.
    write a dissertation
    write up a dissertation
    hand in a dissertation
    complete a dissertation
    She spent three years writing her doctoral dissertation.
    The student defended his dissertation successfully.
    Her dissertation focused on medieval literature.
  2. A lengthy lecture on a subject; a treatise; a discourse; a sermon.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • diss (clipping)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • all but dissertation
  • dissertational
  • dissertationist
  • dissertator
  • doctoral dissertation
  • predissertation

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin dissertātiōnem, from dissertō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /di.sɛʁ.ta.sjɔ̃/
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

dissertation f (plural dissertations)

  1. dissertation, essay
    Synonyms: essai, composition, rédaction

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Dutch: dissertatie
    • → Indonesian: disertasi

Further reading

[edit]
  • “dissertation”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
